text: {"score":4,"justification":"Numbers match the card: 27.5% of 240 claims, expected 4.8%, risk-adjusted score 5.74, z 3.76, 7 of 9 documented 99215 claims below billed (78%), 5 of 21 with no lab line, 30 records returned. The 24% low-complexity share is correct. The cited claims fit their sentences: C0086162, C0086180 and C0086251 appear in examples_below_billed, and C0086163, C0086166 and C0086174 are low-complexity 99215 claims. The language is cautious (\"a reason to review the records, not a finding\"), and the summary notes that no audit trail was received. The next steps are concrete: request charts, have a coder re-score, and avoid extrapolating from a targeted sample. Weaknesses: the unmatched \"10\" comes from the note-check percentages (problems 10%, data 10%), which the card does not show but which probably come from tool output. The 14% comparison rate is the all-provider rate of 0.143, so it is fine. The summary does not say which documented 99215 claims were supported (C0086228 and C0086410, both high MDM). It also lists only three of the below-billed claims out of seven, and it shows no contrast with high-complexity patients. The audit trail request is odd given that none was received, and the note-check line is somewhat noisy. Overall it is accurate and actionable, with minor gaps.","problems":["Number 10 (note-check percentages) is not on the evidence card; its support depends on tool output","Does not mention the 2 supported 99215 claims (C0086228, C0086410), so the picture is one-sided","Examples cover only 3 of the 7 below-billed claims","Next step asks for the audit trail even though the summary says none was received, and does not explain why","The note-check percentages are given with little interpretation"]}
